_comment: SN60's deployment settings. Read by kata-subnets-deploy's installer, which validates every
value against its allowlist and ceilings before rendering any unit. This file may set only
what a subnet decides for itself: challenge sizing, its own budget caps, and round timing.
Lane identity, source repo, plugin path, entry point, writable paths and public visibility are
the registry's; naming one here is refused outright, not ignored.
subnet_id and lane_id below are an ASSERTION, not an input: they are checked against the
registry lane so pointing the generator at the wrong checkout fails loudly.

KATA_SUBNET_BUDGET_TEE_RUNS is the hard room-execution dimension. Worst case for one challenge is projects x replicas x 2 contestants x room attempts = 7 x 3 x 2 x 3 = 126, so 1260 is ten challenges a day. The agent's inference remains miner-funded inside the room; the separate Bitsec scoring judge is validator-funded and is bounded by the KATA_SN60_JUDGE_* per-challenge gateway plus the daily inference-call cap.

KATA_SUBNET_BUDGET_INFERENCE_CALLS is the judge's daily backstop and must be one challenge's worst case times the SAME ten challenges TEE_RUNS allows, because a reservation is checked as used + reserved + worst case: a day cap equal to KATA_SN60_JUDGE_MAX_CALLS would run one round per UTC day and defer the rest however little they actually spent, and a budget defer is a healthy no-op that reads as an idle lane rather than a misconfiguration. 5000 x 10 = 50000. This exceeds what a lane may normally self-declare; the installer's ceiling was raised deliberately for it (see kata-subnets-deploy MAX_BUDGET_BY_ENV).

KATA_SN60_JUDGE_MAX_CALLS is the per-challenge hard ceiling the gateway enforces. Measured worst case is 3600 = the benchmark's seven most expensive projects (600 judge calls at expected x ceil(eval_max_vulns / chunk_size)) x 3 replicas x 2 contestants, so 5000 leaves ~39% headroom. Recalculate it whenever the sample size, replica count or the benchmark's expected-finding counts change.

KATA_SN60_SANDBOX_ROOT is deliberately EMPTY, not absent. The lane now scores the manifest-verified tree vendored with the plugin, and empty means 'use it'. The unit loads /srv/kata-bot/.env BEFORE this file, so a stale KATA_SN60_SANDBOX_ROOT=/srv/sandbox left on a host would otherwise survive the retirement and win -- pointing the lane back at the clone it no longer keeps. Setting it here overrides that; deleting the line does not.

KATA_SN60_PROXY_IMAGE_DIGEST pins the scoring proxy by immutable image id. Upstream builds it as the MUTABLE tag bitsec-proxy:latest from whatever is on the host, carrying no record of its origin, so two hosts can serve different judges under one name. Rebuild with tools/build_proxy_image.py -- which verifies the vendored tree FIRST and stamps the sandbox commit and tree digest into image labels -- then set this to the digest it prints and restart the proxy. The lane re-checks digest AND labels before spending, so a proxy built from a different scorer revision fails the round closed.

The scorer dependency environment lives outside the verified sandbox and is reused only when its uv.lock fingerprint matches. /srv/kata is already writable in the hardened unit; no write access to the verified source is required.

submission_policy is THIS SUBNET's answer to a question the competition repository's PR gate has to ask: may a submission reach the network itself? Declared here because it is a property of this subnet's agent contract, not of the gate.
The gate cannot import this repository -- it runs on a bare Python with no pip install -- so kata-subnets-deploy publishes this into the competition repo as data. See docs/contracts.md.
